newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks firmer ahead of credit rating.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks firmer ahead of credit rating.

text.p: Croatian stocks continued to firm with blue chips scoring new records on Thursday, as the country waited for its first credit rating.
Traders said interest from international investors, counting on a solid rating, would boost prices of most liquid issues. It is expected to be announced later on Thursday or Friday.
"Croatia is finally on the map of foreign buyers," said Nenad Pavletic of Auctor brokerage and predicted brisker trade in very near future.
Seven of 12 active issues rose on Thursday, one fell and four remained stable. Volume halved to 5,582 shares, turnover also slipped to 2.9 million kuna.
Blue chips drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka broke all previous records after their GDRs soared in London Wednesday.

Zagrebacka closed at 1,700 kuna, up 100 but off the all-time high of 1,800 kuna earlier in the session. The volume was relatively small on 541 units due to scarce offer, traders said, casting doubts on whether the current price could hold.
It was the first time its Zagreb price had overshot London, where it traded at $29.625 per 1/10 GDR on Seaq International.
Pliva added 50 kuna to 540 with 1,160 kuna changing hands. Its GDRs fetched $18.7/80 on the London Stock Exchange.
Top gainer was Zagrebacka's preference E-series stock, jumping 150 kuna to close at 950, with 277 shares sold.
It rose 50 percent over the last three days after investors realised it carried a fixed dividend of 7.0 percent on face value of 100 German marks, said Josko Milisa at I.F.C brokers.
Hoteliers Istraturist and Jadranturist added 10 kuna each to close at 200 and 290 kuna, respectively, on volumes of 1,104 and 119 shares.
The price of Jadranturist and chocolate maker Kras, flat at 490 kuna, was seen as fluctuating in the months ahead.
Pavletic predicted livelier trading in stocks that have been neglected so far, such as cable maker Elka and Adriatic pipeline Janaf, particularly ahead of its flotation.
Elka was also among gainers, adding 10 kuna to close at 190 on volume of 125 units. Textile firm Varteks gained 14.90 kuna to 107, selling 108 shares in its first deal since last April.
Food processor Podravka closed flat at 264 kuna, after trading 2,139 shares in a 260-65 kuna range. Traders said it was Croatia's most stable stock at the moment.
The only loser hotelier Suncani Hvar edged down four kuna to 60, selling 108 shares.
